note: Every WebSocket close the relay, the browser and the host send, and what each implementation does on receiving a code, as of 2026-11-12 (relay with the pre-auth cap). Nothing here is a decided value: today one code, 1008, carries every refusal, including the benign peer-replaced. A reason is the exact close reason string; an empty string means no reason. Only the reasons in relayReasons are constants in the relay code; the other reasons are literals there.

closes.cause: the peer sent bye
the version probe got its hello-ok
no hello within the hello deadline, or a viewer's proof past the proof deadline
a host's register-proof past the proof deadline
malformed or unexpected hello or proof, bad role, token or identity, oversize or non-text before the session is live, signaling ticket or epoch refused
the viewer's identity proof did not verify
the viewer is not on the PC's admission list and offered no pairing code
wrong pairing code or no pairing window open
too many failed pairing attempts
a data socket's ticket or epoch was not accepted
a live socket sent a packet the relay does not accept, or a data socket's epoch is no longer current
the host's admit list no longer contains this connected viewer
a newer socket of the same role, PC and epoch connected
the admin deleted the PC
the site gate did not approve this browser socket (accepted, then closed)
the socket could not be restored after the relay woke from hibernation
idle past the idle deadline, or a message over the read limit after the hello
the viewer's signaling socket left
the other end of the file pair left
the host registered a new media epoch
the PC table could not be persisted
the send queue overflowed (native server only)
a socket that had not finished its hello or proof was dropped to make room
the viewer ended the session
no answer to a media ping within the dead limit; no other implementation defines or handles 4000
the host closes its sockets with no code

clientActions.note: What the receiver of a close does. terminal: the session ends and is not retried. retry: reconnect with that implementation's own backoff. restart-attempt: the whole connection attempt (both sockets) restarts. end-run: the host's serve run ends and the serve loop retries with its backoff.

host.media: retry until the refusal limit, then refused; ends for good when the reason contains stale or retired (a text match on the reason)

userMessages.note: What the viewer shows on a terminal 1008, whatever the reason. admitted: the session had finished the handshake.

browser.notAdmitted: Not admitted, with the relay's reason appended

unpinned.clientWin: classify() in session.rs is private to the session module; no test outside it can call it
unpinned.host: close_verdict() in wss_v4.rs is private; its own unit test covers the 1008 and stale cases
unpinned.relayEmission: the sans-IO relay is driven only by its own harness; reasons are pinned as constants, not by driving every refusal path
